extracted.intended_audience: Coast Guard managers, contracting officers, policy analysts, and researchers studying A-76 contracting/outsource reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of U.S. Coast Guard implementation of OMB Circular A-76 (management study, PWS, MEO, contracting, and post-award administration) including causes of cost increases and effects on workforce and billets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management study 'team effort' staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: The management study should be a 'team effort' using persons with expertise in management analysis, staffing, position classification, work measurement, value engineering, industrial engineering, cost analysis, contracting, and technical aspects of the functional effort under study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB Circular A-76 supplement discusses the management study as a team effort; criticism arises when the study is assigned as a collateral duty to a person without the skill or experience, which adds time and can produce inaccurate PWS and MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely completion of MEO/cost studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies must be completed within realistic time requirements; GAO found DOD averaged two years per MEO cost study with some taking up to eight years, and many studies ongoing for six or more years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unrealistic timeframes and insufficient staffing contribute to long completion times; Coast Guard had shorter average times in one review (only 14 of 100 took >2 years), but rushed deadlines at unit level can produce incomplete reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation quality of Performance Work Statement (PWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: PWSs must be complete, specific, and include adequate quality assurance plans; vague PWSs or omitted tasks lead to poor initial contracts and later contract add-ons/cost increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: some initial food service PWSs were vague with poor QA plans; contract specialists say incomplete PWSs can be usable with additional inquiry, but poor PWSs have led to increased costs when items are added to contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEO (Most Efficient Organization) cost determination accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: MEO cost determinations must be prepared accurately; lack of skilled personnel to develop the MEO and proper cost analyses leads to errors and extended study times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers without proper training and experience often produce inaccurate MEOs; headquarters guidance and sample studies alone may be insufficient to ensure accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualifications and staffing (avoid collateral duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel assigned to conduct A-76 reviews should possess requisite skills and experience rather than performing reviews as collateral duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coast Guard often shifted burden to field units where the reviewer lacked proper skills; training supplements and example studies are not substitutes for experienced staff, and this can lengthen studies and reduce quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination between Headquarters and Contract Administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective coordination between Headquarters (review staff) and Contract Administrators (e.g., MLCPAC) is necessary to produce complete PWSs and manage solicitations, especially for geographically distributed activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distance between review sites and study team contributed to incomplete PWSs; limited coordination between Headquarters and MLCPAC caused solicitation/administration issues for Pacific Area contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTR (Contracting Officer's Technical Representative) competence and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: COTRs and QA evaluators must be experienced, attentive, and properly trained; short tours or inadequate attention/skill can weaken the link between contract requirements and performance oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military COTRs often serve 2-3 years and may lack experience; Coast Guard provides 1–5 day courses but these are not a substitute for experience. Example: contractor giving away free breakfasts was not caught by COTR oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance follow-through (COTR must enforce QA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Assurance (QA) procedures in contracts must be actively enforced by COTRs rather than relying solely on contractor assertions that work was completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Base Honolulu, QA was not followed up by the COTR who took the contractor's word; adequate QA implementation is critical and COTR must not simply accept contractor claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use best available cost data for savings estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of expected cost savings should be based on the best available cost data, not standardized assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO found DOD used standardized assumptions rather than best data; this contributes to inaccurate reported savings. Agencies should collect and analyze actual cost information after implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine post-implementation cost tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must routinely collect and analyze cost information to monitor actual operations after a cost study and while contracts are in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD did not routinely collect such information; Coast Guard likewise did not track contract cost increases unless a major performance problem occurred, leading to unreliable savings measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include study and implementation costs when calculating savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculations of A-76 cost savings should include the costs of doing the study, preparing the PWS, developing the MEO, and the costs of implementing the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coast Guard and DOD often omitted these implementation/study costs from savings figures; omitting them inflates perceived savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain accurate and complete savings databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated systems and databases used to accumulate expected cost savings must contain accurate and complete information and must calculate totals correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO identified inaccurate/incomplete information and miscalculations in DOD's computerized database; such flaws undermine assessments of true savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for contract life cost increases in savings analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost increases that occur during the life of a contract (e.g., wage determinations, modifications) must be considered when assessing whether contracting-out remains cost-effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coast Guard computed average annual cost savings from initial estimates and did not account for later cost increases; in examples (housing, food service, guard), DOL wage determinations were primary drivers of increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid omitted tasks that lead to add-ons and cost growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure contract specifications/PWS include all necessary tasks to avoid later additions to contracts that increase costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO review of 20 DOD functions found poorly prepared PWSs with omitted tasks led to added items and cost increases; although many still realized savings, omissions create management problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage workforce perception and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must manage perceptions that A-76 equals pure contracting-out with loss of billets, communicate the MEO concept, and avoid incentivizing undercutting of MEOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor perception reduces acceptance and may lead reviewers/commanders to undercut MEOs to 'win' competitions; this can produce an MEO that cannot properly carry out duties if implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide workforce protections and placement efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 requires agencies to exert 'maximum effort' to place adversely affected employees, including priority for available positions, reemployment priority lists, reasonable training and relocation costs, and coordination with OPM and Department of Labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed protections per OMB Circular: priority for agency positions, reemployment lists, pay for training/relocation related to placement, coordination with OPM/DoL, right of first refusal for contract positions when qualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess multi-mission impacts on employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Management studies must include a multi-mission impact statement to assess the impact of potential billet deletions and contracting-out on affected employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COMDT (G-CPP-2) required a multi-mission impact statement as part of the study to address employee effects; this is part of improved coordination with workforce planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor effects on enlisted ratings and billet structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and monitor how contracting-out affects specific enlisted ratings (e.g., Subsistence Specialist, Electronics Technician) and sea/shore rotation, advancement, and retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: SS billets were heavily reduced, altering sea/shore rotation and hurting retention/recruitment; program managers developed action plans to address rate-specific impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure contract specifications are not open to varying interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract specifications should be precise to avoid differing interpretations that can create disputes or poor performance outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base Honolulu noted past contract specifications were 'too vague and open to interpretation' which both parties saw as a problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administration proximity and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Distance and communication delays between contract administration offices and unit-level COTRs/customers can hinder effective contract administration and responsiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MLCPAC distance to Base Honolulu caused slow responses; reliance on letters/telephone without direct observation led to discrepancies in perceived contract performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and document contract modifications and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain detailed modification histories and explicitly document reasons for modifications (e.g., funding shortfalls, wage determinations, scope expansions) to understand cost trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example Table III documents a series of modifications and extensions with dates and remarks; tracking these shows wage determinations and continuing resolutions drove increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize learning curve improvements but not rely on them
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial errors in PWS and contract preparation may improve over time (learning curve), but initial poor practices should not be tolerated as acceptable practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coast Guard acknowledged earlier errors improved through experience, but initial vagueness caused poor contracts and increased costs; training/experienced staff remain necessary.
